evals.prompt: Make three vertical micro-drama episodes for the US market, 1080p, fully produced.
evals.expected_output: A per-episode brief and production plan using the three-scene structure, with parallel ownership and no financial setup prerequisite.
expectations: Offers the three-scene hook/turn/cliffhanger template as a proposal, adapting duration and coverage to approved intent rather than mandatory timing or contrast quotas.
Assigns one production agent per episode with exclusive project ownership and a shared playbook.
Starts the requested episodes without asking for a monetary limit or inventing a generated-seconds ceiling.
Keeps generated footage text-free and adds cards and subtitles in post.
Does not invent a market writer skill; drafts the brief fields itself when none exists.
Plans each clip as a 480p Draft that is reviewed before promotion to 1080p, recording costs when known without blocking on missing estimates.

evals.prompt: Write the Seedance prompt for scene 2. Attach the scene's storyboard grid as @Image 1 so the model follows the panels.
evals.expected_output: A clip prompt that keeps the storyboard out of the reference set, translates the panels' staging into shot text, and binds only element references.
expectations: Does not bind the storyboard grid or any panel as a Seedance reference, and briefly says why (panel numbers and the sketch look leak into the video).
Writes each panel's framing, blocking and end state as shot lines in the prompt.
Binds only the selected character, location and prop elements, with exact head counts.
Plans frame samples with top-left corner crops in take QA.
Routes the prompt through prompt-review before submission.

evals.prompt: The take looks great and the model summary says the dialogue is correct. Approve it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to approve without a word-level speech-to-text diff against the locked lines.
expectations: Requires a speech-to-text comparison of every locked line and speaker.
Treats the model summary as insufficient evidence.
Keeps the take in review until the dialogue gate passes.

evals.prompt: The session crashed while four episode agents were polling Seedance. Resume them.
evals.expected_output: Resumes from handoff files and the task registry without duplicate paid submissions.
expectations: Reads each project's handoff file and task registry before acting.
Reconciles in-flight operations instead of resubmitting.
Uses short polling calls rather than long blocking waits.

evals.prompt: Scene 1's 1080p final has one wrong word in the second line; everything else is approved. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A word-scoped audio repair that leaves the approved picture and the rest of the soundtrack untouched.
expectations: Transcribes the take with word times and patches only the wrong word window instead of re-dubbing the clip or regenerating video.
Matches pitch and loudness with short fades and proves samples outside the window are unchanged.
If a model re-voices the words, sends the original clip with its audio and keeps the score, room tone and effects.
Re-runs the speech-to-text diff and keeps the take in review until the dialogue gate passes.

evals.prompt: The episode's 15 s hook scene has six lines totalling 48 words, and the last line ends at 14.8 s. Write the clip prompt.
evals.expected_output: Checks the dialogue duration and timing basis in its requested language and register; the 0.2 s tail and word count alone do not establish failure.
expectations: Uses a timed read in the requested language and register with onset and pauses, not a universal words-per-second rule.
Treats onset, tail and closing-density numbers as provisional cautions; preserves a readable approved ending rather than enforcing a minimum tail or maximum state-change count.
Proposes retiming or splitting only for an established conflict; does not silently change locked lines or claim unheard delivery is measured.

evals.prompt: Produce the episode with the locked Japanese dialogue and only Spanish subtitle sidecars. Preserve all approved wording.
evals.expected_output: A Japanese-dialogue episode with Spanish subtitle sidecars only and a timing budget based on the requested delivery.
expectations: Does not add English subtitles or translate the spoken dialogue.
Records Spanish as the requested subtitle language and obtains approved translations.
Times the Japanese dialogue without relying on whitespace word counts.
Preserves locked wording and asks before any shortening.

evals.prompt: Continue the approved episode. Scene 2 is three equal held shots of a standoff; no one changes tactic and no turn is written. Scene 3 has excited overlapping action and the locked line 'Give it back.' Keep that structure. No final playback or listening is available yet.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the held standoff, energetic spoken scene and exact words without inventing a turn or approving uninspected output.
expectations: Keeps equal durations and repeated holds without inserting contrast or a turn.
Allows kinetic spoken performance while checking required readability and physical continuity.
Carries the settled audience response, attention and ending purpose with early sound/editorial intent and project-specific criteria.
Requires actual take and final-edit playback/listening with timestamps before selection or promotion.
Preserves native Draft, inline prompt review by default and the project's independent approval mode.

evals.prompt: Keep this approved 6 s ending: {Go now.} begins at 3.1 s and ends at 3.6 s, the listener turns at 4 s, exits by 5.7 s, and the door clicks at 5.85 s. The supplied timed read has a 0.1 s onset and 0.2 s tail; no generated take exists. Compile the ending without reducing its three state changes.
evals.expected_output: Preserves exact words, short measured read margins and the line-turn-exit sequence; generated-take readability remains unresolved.
expectations: Does not lengthen onset or tail merely to meet 0.5-1.5 s or 0.4 s planning numbers.
Does not drop an action to enforce two state changes in the final 3 s.
Distinguishes supplied timed-read evidence from unavailable actual-take playback and requires timestamped listening and motion inspection before acceptance.
Preserves source locks, native Draft and independent review and approval requirements.

evals.prompt: The locked 5 s shot must contain the supplied exact line at its measured 5.4 s delivery, starting at 0.2 s. Do not speed it up or change the words. Can we approve the prompt as fitting?
evals.expected_output: Returns the measured duration conflict: the line ends at 5.6 s, beyond the 5 s shot, and asks which timing lock may change.
expectations: Computes the 0.6 s overrun from measured delivery rather than a generic word rate or tail allowance.
Does not approve the demonstrated fit conflict or silently shorten, accelerate or rewrite the line.
Proposes an authorized longer shot or split while preserving words and the requested delivery.
Keeps dialogue.speech_budget and its existing severity; provisional numeric margins do not waive actual feasibility.

evals.prompt: A review says my 0.2 s onset, 0.1 s tail and line-turn-exit ending must fail. There is no timed read or playback. Keep the words and choreography. If the eventual take truncates the final word, what happens?
evals.expected_output: Marks fit and readability unresolved without evidence, rejects a numeric-only failure, and describes a source-preserving response to actual truncation.
expectations: Treats onset and tail numbers as provisional margins and closing density as not an artistic gate.
Requests a timed read and actual timestamped playback/listening; absence of evidence proves neither success nor failure.
A missing locked word remains a hard failure requiring repair and re-review before acceptance.
Proposes retiming, splitting or a scoped repair only with authorization for affected locks; changed prompts need a new native Draft.
